video.title: I Found the Perfect First Business for Introverts

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Ryan Schuetter, a 24-26 year old introverted Cincinnati ex-hospital project manager ($52k/yr) who now earns roughly $10-15k/month as an AI implementation consultant and educator. He started by having ~100-150 free, non-salesy video calls with people in his personal network and business groups, converting about 12 into paying clients (~$25k lifetime from the first 12). His offers are private AI coaching ($5-10k/month), month-long cohort groups ($1,000 per seat), and one-off implementation builds ($1k-$20k), organised around his DASA framework (Diagnose, Articulate, Systemize, AI). Key takeaway: relationship-led, value-first outreach plus education and free content can win clients without sales experience, though the model is human-led and network-dependent.

speakers.description: 24-26 year old AI implementation consultant and educator in Cincinnati, Ohio

ideas.name: AI implementation consulting and education for small businesses (Ryan's overall business)
ideas.one_liner: Introvert-friendly consultancy that helps founders and small businesses adopt AI through coaching, cohorts and custom builds.
ideas.business_model: Mix of monthly retainer coaching, one-off cohort fees and project-based build fees.
ideas.customer: Founders and small/medium business owners (pre-revenue to ~$20M revenue, mostly under $10M) who understand AI's power but whose teams are not using it; also managers and department leaders.
ideas.problem: Teams are not adopting AI effectively; owners are not tech-savvy and cannot identify which problems AI should solve.
ideas.offer: Free discovery calls and lead-magnet resources leading to paid private coaching, cohort sprints and implementation builds, guided by the DASA framework.

pricing.model: Tiered: high-ticket monthly coaching, per-seat cohort, hourly-based project pricing

price_points.label: Internal hourly rate used to price builds

pricing.notes: Builds priced on $200/hour times estimated hours; early projects $500-$1,000.

acquisition_channels.details: Personal network: phone contacts, LinkedIn connections, friends' parents, ex-colleagues; rekindling messages with several casual texts before mentioning AI; ~100 free calls over ~3 months, 3-4x as many reach-outs as calls booked; still texts/calls 10 people daily.

quote.text: I would send, you know, a batch of a hundred texts in the morning or emails or however, you know, LinkedIn DMs, wherever.
quote.speaker: Ryan Schuetter

acquisition_channels.details: Two local groups (business group, Cincy AI meetup) and two online masterminds of ~500 members; online groups produced most paying customers via long-standing relationships.
Unpolished screen-recorded demos and tutorials (about 100 subscribers, most videos ~30 views) sent to prospects as proof and credibility.

quote.text: Doesn't matter if the video has 30 views or 30,000. Most have 30.
quote.speaker: Ryan Schuetter

acquisition_channels.details: Lead magnets (prompt frameworks, SEO guides, how-to-use Claude Code) and workshops sent after calls; newsletter on Substack starting; repeated re-engagement loops.
Mass email outreach was tried and produced nothing.

quote.text: I did attempt to do the, you know, mass email outreach. Nothing happened with it. Zero.
quote.speaker: Ryan Schuetter

ideas.delivery: Ryan personally delivers: ~10 hrs/week for one private coaching client; weekly group lesson plus end-of-week call plus 30-min one-on-ones for cohorts (~10 hrs/week); custom builds (AI tools, marketing/sales tools, CRM/automation setups) done by him using Claude, n8n, GoHighLevel etc.
unit_economics_claims: First 12 clients ~ $25k lifetime from ~350 hours (~$50-100/hr in his figure)
One advisory client paid ~ $15k over a year
ideas.startup_cost: About $20 (a month of an AI tool subscription)
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: About 3 months of free calls before first ~$500-$1,000 projects; majority of paid deals came from third conversations

acquisition.how: Relationship texting/calls and meetups are human-led; only drafting messages, lead-magnet content and CRM follow-up could be tooled. Cold outreach to individuals is restricted under UK PECR.

onboarding.how: Intake forms, scheduling and resource delivery can be automated, but discovery conversations (DASA diagnose/articulate) are human.

delivery.how: Coaching, cohort teaching and bespoke builds are founder-delivered live; agents can assist building but the trust-based advisory is human.

billing.how: Stripe invoices/subscriptions and payment links are easily automated.

support.how: Ongoing relationship and advice is human; routine questions could be handled by agents.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in the UK; network-led selling is legal. Mass cold DMs/texts to individuals or sole traders would breach PECR, though personal-contact outreach is fine. Prices and the UK market for AI consultants are different; GDPR applies to client data.

risks: Heavily dependent on founder's time and personal network; income was lumpy (months with no money)
Many competitors ('AI bros'); skepticism from small business owners
Security risk of tools like OpenClaw given access to business systems
Low hourly return in the first months (~$2/hr in early stage)

tactics.name: 100 free value-first calls with your existing network
steps: List contacts from phone, LinkedIn, ex-colleagues, family friends and business groups
Research each person's recent news on LinkedIn/Facebook and send a genuine rekindling message with no pitch
Exchange several casual messages before mentioning AI
Send batches of ~100 messages in the morning and reply through the day
Offer a free 1-hour Google Meet to provide value; aim for 100 real conversations (needed 3-4x reach-outs)
Do not sell on call one; send takeaways and lead magnets
Keep re-engaging with follow-ups and useful tidbits over months

quote.text: I was just trying to get on the phone and provide value in any way I can. I'm not trying to pitch anything.
quote.speaker: Ryan Schuetter

tactics.name: Let offers emerge from conversations
steps: Use free calls to learn what people value and what you're good at
Notice that education was valued most
Package into coaching, cohorts and builds
Start with a one-person trial cohort, then scale

quote.text: this came from what I learned on the free calls with people.
quote.speaker: Ryan Schuetter

tactics.name: Lead magnet loop with unpolished YouTube content
steps: Record screen demos and tutorials in one take without heavy editing
Build prompt frameworks, SEO guides and Claude Code guides as reusable resources
Send the relevant resource after each call
Share niche-targeted videos to re-engage dormant contacts

quote.text: a lot of these resources and guides, for instance, are like prompt frameworks, their SEO guides, their how to use clawed code.
quote.speaker: Ryan Schuetter

tactics.name: DASA framework
steps: Diagnose: find the real problem worth solving
Articulate: describe the dream outcome (time saved or money made)
Systemize: gather SOPs and design the working process
AI: only then implement AI
Calls 1-2 cover Diagnose and Articulate; Systemize and AI happen post-close

quote.text: if you're automating chaos, you're scaling chaos.
quote.speaker: Ryan Schuetter

tactics.name: Elicit real problems with better questions
steps: Ask 'what is keeping you up at night?'
Ask follow-up 'why' questions
Research the business beforehand and ask about specific offerings
Use unexpected questions to get past polite answers

quote.text: I love asking like what is the thing that is haunting you
quote.speaker: Ryan Schuetter

tactics.name: Daily 10 outreach to build the next cohort
steps: Pick a deliverable to teach
Text or call 10 contacts per day inviting them to join
Frame it as building alongside other business owners
Repeat continuously to avoid sales funnel stalls

quote.text: I reach out to 10 people every day doing the same thing I've been doing for the past year.
quote.speaker: Ryan Schuetter

tactics.name: Give away the playbook to win repeat work
steps: Teach the exact build process in cohorts
Show clients results
They return for further projects and advice

quote.text: I give every old thing away.
quote.speaker: Ryan Schuetter

quote.speaker: Ryan Schuetter

lessons.lesson: Your existing network is a large, underused sales channel; warm outreach beats cold at tiny scale (about 8% close from ~150 warm conversations).

quote.text: People underestimate how many people they actually have in their sphere.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Removing the selling goal ('I just want to help') lowers pressure for introverts and builds trust that converts later, often on the third conversation.

quote.text: it's way easier if you're not trying to sell.
quote.speaker: Ryan Schuetter

lessons.lesson: Early hourly returns can be terrible (~$2/hr); the real payoff is relationships, testimonials and offer discovery.

quote.text: you're building something for yourself and that's the whole point.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Don't over-engineer tooling or CRM before you have traction; send the messages first.

quote.text: There's no reason to it because you're going to learn along the way
quote.speaker: Ryan Schuetter

lessons.lesson: Education and cohort offers let a solo operator sell many seats at once (about $250/hr effective) while building proof and follow-on implementation work.
In-person networking is a differentiator versus the many online-only AI sellers and is likely to raise close rates.

quote.text: when you're in person, then you're in the 1%.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Publishing low-production proof (demos, videos) gives credibility without needing a degree or audience.

quote.text: I don't need a degree to prove that I could do these things.
quote.speaker: Ryan Schuetter

lessons.lesson: Giving away know-how tends to produce more paid work rather than less because clients come back with further problems.
Ask sharper, more emotional questions (what keeps you up at night) to surface problems owners can't articulate.
Income from a personal-relationship model is lumpy; consistent daily outreach is needed to smooth it.

evidence_quality.rationale: First-hand operator with concrete process and prices, but income figures are self-reported, the best month is projected, much revenue came from a few clients and the model is network-dependent. Host adds hypothetical math.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Host sells the Playmakers AI community and promotes GoHighLevel and Beehive via sponsor reads; Ryan sells coaching and cohorts.
